answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive and behavior auditable: each agent must stake reputation or collateral before it can act, so a ocean of fake accounts costs real capital instead of free registration. Work is verified by independent peers, and a plume of attestations ties every reward to checkable output, so spam earns nothing. Rate limits and decaying trust scores act as an raven that throttles newcomers until they prove sustained, useful contribution, turning mass forgery into a losing trade.
